theater: 埃里溫、卡爾斯與阿拉斯河谷

battle.name: 奧斯曼-波斯戰爭 (1821年-1823年)
battle.theater: 埃里溫、卡爾斯與阿拉斯河谷
battle.brief: 一八二一年起，奧斯曼帝國為切斷俄羅斯伸入高加索，兵出埃爾祖魯姆與卡爾斯，圍攻埃里溫、嘉尼一帶的波斯汗國；波斯王儲阿巴斯米爾扎隨即在阿拉斯河谷反攻，雙方拉鋸至一八二三年。火繩槍仍係兩軍步兵骨幹，線形列陣、分段齊射，撐住攻守兩線的消耗。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 交戰的兩方是奧斯曼帝國與卡札爾波斯，戰線同時鋪在安納托利亞東境、高加索東南與伊拉克三個方向。奧斯曼方面由蘇丹馬哈茂德二世在伊斯坦布爾坐鎮，前線以「帕夏—軍團—營」逐級分派：埃爾祖魯姆、卡爾斯與凡城三省的守軍由各自總督率領，安納托利亞與魯梅利亞的常備步兵由禁衛軍與各近衛步兵團充任，克里米亞可汗國的騎兵與其附庸諾曼人被徵發北上，巴格達、摩蘇爾與基爾庫克則歸伊拉克軍區節制。波斯方面由卡札爾沙法特阿里沙坐鎮德黑蘭，王儲阿巴斯米爾扎領御林軍與北方各省騎兵，樞密院大臣米爾扎·阿卜杜勒哈桑汗掌西線；埃里溫、嘉尼、卡拉巴赫、希爾萬等高加索汗國名義上仍效忠波斯，但自一八一三年《古利斯坦條約》後已受俄羅斯監督，守軍多懷兩面應付之心。兩套指揮系統的效率差距——奧斯曼的文書與軍令雖繁複卻能逐級落實，波斯的命令常止於王儲與樞密院、難以及於游散的部落民兵——是這場戰爭裡最易被忽略、卻最要命的一環。
countriesEn: The two parties were the Ottoman Empire and Qajar Persia, and the fighting front ran at the same time along the eastern Anatolian border, in the south-eastern Caucasus, and in Iraq. On the Ottoman side Sultan Mahmud II held the centre in Istanbul, and the front was allotted in a strict pasha-corps-battalion chain: the garrison provinces of Erzurum, Kars and Van answered to their own governors; the standing infantry of Anatolia and Rumelia was furnished by the Janissaries and the various household infantry regiments; Crimean Tatar cavalry and their Nogai auxiliaries were levied to the north; and Baghdad, Mosul and Kirkuk fell under the Iraqi military district. On the Persian side the Qajar Shah Fath-Ali Shah sat in Tehran, the crown prince Abbas Mirza led the household troops and the cavalry levies of the northern provinces, and the grand vizier Mirza Abolhassan Khan took charge of the western front. The Caucasian khanates of Erivan, Ganja, Karabakh and Shirvan still claimed a nominal allegiance to Persia, but since the Treaty of Gulistan of 1813 they had been under Russian supervision, and their garrisons were inclined to serve two masters at once. The difference in the efficiency of the two command systems - the Ottoman chain, cumbersome in paperwork yet able to deliver an order down to the unit, against the Persian system, whose orders often stopped at the crown prince and the vizier and seldom reached the wandering tribal levies - is the most easily overlooked and at the same time the most fatal feature of this war.
people: 人物上，蘇丹馬哈茂德二世是奧斯曼方面的最高決策者，他在拿破崙戰爭結束後把國策重新轉向東方，並於一八二一年下令出兵；具體的前線指揮則分交各路帕夏，卡爾斯與埃爾祖魯姆方向由當地駐軍主將統率，凡城方向與巴格達方向的戰役由抵達後再行分兵的高級官員接手。波斯方面，卡札爾沙法特阿里沙在德黑蘭遙控戰局，但真正在北方作戰的是王儲阿巴斯米爾扎：他既要在高加索頂住奧斯曼的推進，又要抽調兵力應付西線與阿富汗方向，因此常被迫在兩個戰場之間分兵，這正是波斯屢屢失分的關鍵。樞密院大臣米爾扎·阿卜杜勒哈桑汗以老練著稱，負責伊拉克與庫爾迪斯坦方向，戰事後期奉命東進支援，成為西線的支柱；他在戰後轉往克爾曼沙赫應付阿富汗方向的壓力。外國方面，英國駐德黑蘭領事金尼爾一系所寫的報告，是當時少數可用的第三方觀察，記錄了波斯軍隊的士氣、軍需與沿途情形；俄羅斯雖未公開派兵，卻以邊境管束與武器買賣影響戰局，說明這場戰爭自始至終都擺在「大問題」的陰影之下。
peopleEn: On the Ottoman side the supreme decision rested with Sultan Mahmud II, who turned the empire's policy back to the east once the Napoleonic Wars were over and gave the order to march in 1821; the actual command on the ground was distributed among the provincial pashas, with the garrisons of Kars and Erzurum led by their own incumbents, and the fighting around Van and around Baghdad handed to senior officers who arrived with reinforcements and then split their forces. On the Persian side Fath-Ali Shah directed affairs from Tehran, but the man who actually fought in the north was the crown prince Abbas Mirza: he had to hold the Ottomans off in the Caucasus while simultaneously stripping troops away for the western front and for the Afghan frontier, and he was therefore constantly forced to divide his army between two theatres - the very reason for the repeated Persian set-backs. The grand vizier Mirza Abolhassan Khan, noted for his long experience, handled Iraq and Kurdistan and was later ordered east to shore up the western line; after the war he was shifted to Kermanshah to meet the pressure from Afghanistan. On the foreign side the reports written by the British consular circle in Tehran, of which those of Kinneir and his colleagues are the best known, form one of the few third-party observations available and record the morale, the supply situation and the condition of the roads along the Persian line. Russia did not openly send troops, yet it shaped the course of the war through frontier control and the arms trade, which shows that the conflict was fought from the first day to the last under the shadow of the larger Eastern Question.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是十六世紀初已定型的西班牙式長身火繩槍。火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊，方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕 - 這句話正是本役的實況。火繩槍的弱點很明顯：槍身沉重，射手須以叉架或依托支撐，瞄準要靠火繩燃燒的節奏去配合照門，風勢、雨雪與濕氣都會令火繩熄滅，單兵裝填緩慢，一分鐘不過數發；它的長處則是價錢低廉、構造簡單、陣地作戰時能形成整齊的彈幕，且不必依賴昂貴的進口火器。奧斯曼方面，禁衛步兵與各近衛步兵團仍大量配發火繩槍，同時混有較新式的燧發槍；守軍在卡爾斯、埃里溫一類要塞的城頭與塹壕之間以火繩槍互相支援，騎兵則攜帶火繩手槍作近戰之用。波斯方面的火繩槍集中於少數成建制的步兵營，兩造名冊常以「托萬奇」指稱這批火繩槍手，火槍多由商隊自俄、英兩地購入，火藥與鉛彈靠沿途城鎮供應；相較之下，波斯騎兵仍以彎刀、長槍與弓箭為主，火槍覆蓋率偏低。除火繩槍之外，兩軍都配備野戰砲與攻城砲：奧斯曼用過二十磅以上的加農砲與臼砲，波斯亦有購自俄國與歐洲商人的銅砲，用於攻守要點；攻城一方還備有坑道、雲梯、衝城槌與拒馬，營帳與帳房器具則隨大營移動。補給方面，糧食、彈藥與修理工具全靠駱駝隊與馬匹馱運，冬令封山時最為艱難。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the long Spanish-pattern matchlock musket as it had been fixed in type by the early sixteenth century. A matchlock has to be lit, aimed and stood in line, and the formation turns those weaknesses into an orderly barrage - a sentence that describes this war exactly. Its weaknesses are plain: the gun is heavy, the shooter must prop it on a rest or some support, aiming depends on the rate of burn of the match cord matched against the sights, wind, rain and damp put the cord out, and a single man can fire only a few rounds a minute. Its advantages are that it is cheap, simple, can produce a disciplined volley when fighting from fixed ground, and does not depend on expensive imported firearms. On the Ottoman side the Janissaries and the household infantry regiments were still largely armed with matchlocks, mixed with newer flintlocks; the garrisons at places such as Kars and Erivan supported one another with matchlock fire between the parapets and the trenches, and the cavalry carried matchlock pistols for close work. On the Persian side the matchlocks were concentrated in a small number of organised infantry units - both sides' rolls call these musket men tofanchi - the guns themselves being bought by merchant caravans from Russia and Britain, with powder and ball coming from the towns on the route. By contrast the Persian cavalry still fought with sabre, long spear and bow, and the rate of musket coverage was low. Beyond the matchlock both armies fielded field and siege guns: the Ottomans used bombards and pieces above twenty pounds, while Persia had copper guns bought from Russia and from European merchants and used them to hold and to attack key points. Besiegers also brought mines, ladders, rams and chevaux-de-frise, and the tent and baggage equipment travelled with the main camp. Supply was the whole difficulty: food, ammunition and repair tools went forward on camel and pack-horse trains, and in winter, when the passes closed, the going was worst of all.
tactics: 火繩槍的技術上限決定了本役的戰術樣板：低射速使每一次齊射的子彈數與整齊度成為唯一可信的火力，因此攻擊多在白日進行，先以砲火打亂敵陣，再由步兵分段射擊。奧斯曼的慣例是把步兵排成密集縱隊，第一排跪地齊射、第二排立射，後續各排依序前進，形成會移動的城牆；騎兵在兩翼衝擊敵陣側背，並反覆衝撞火繩槍尚未裝填的瞬間。這種線形密集的正面壓制在開闊地上有效，在高加索山區卻難以展開，一旦糧秣斷絕或道路被切，縱隊很容易斷成數段。波斯方面以騎兵機動為主：王儲的御林騎兵與各部族民兵善於快速逼近、擾亂然後退走，不與敵人正面纏鬥；但在守城與據點防衛時，坡內的波斯守軍多倚火繩槍與城頭火器居高射擊，並以騎兵不斷襲擊對方的糧道與輜重隊。雙方都懂得避開夜戰 - 火繩槍在黑夜的瞄準與點火幾乎無效，夜間接近與包圍反而成了波斯游騎與奧斯曼輕騎最擅長的活兒。冬天的山區作戰對進攻方更為殘酷：雪封山口、糧草告罄，牲畜大量凍斃，許多戰役並非敗於交火，而是耗在行軍與補給上。
tacticsEn: The technical ceiling of the matchlock dictated the tactical pattern of the whole war: because the rate of fire was low, the only trustworthy output was the number of rounds and the regularity of each volley, so attacks were made in daylight, the artillery first disordering the enemy line and the infantry then firing in successive ranks. Ottoman custom was to draw the foot up in dense columns, the first rank kneeling to fire and the second standing, the following ranks stepping forward in turn to form a moving wall; the cavalry charged the enemy flanks and rear and rode again through the moments when the muskets were not yet reloaded. Such a linear and dense frontal pressure worked well on open ground but could hardly be deployed in the Caucasus mountains, and once the food ran out or the road was cut the column easily broke into separate segments. Persia fought on mobility: the crown prince's household horse and the tribal levies were skilled at coming up fast, troubling the enemy and then breaking away rather than standing in a straight fight; but when holding towns and hill positions the Persian garrison behind the slope relied on matchlocks and heavy pieces firing from above, while the horse kept up attacks on the enemy's supply road and baggage train. Both sides understood the value of avoiding night fighting - aiming and lighting a match in the dark are close to impossible, and night approaches and encircling were the trade of the Persian irregular riders and the Ottoman light horse. Winter campaigning in the mountains was crueller still for the attacker: the passes closed under snow, food ran out, beasts of burden died in numbers, and many operations were not lost in the firing line at all but worn away by marching and supply.
data: 可核實的數字並不多，以下幾項較為可靠。戰事自一八二一年起，至一八二三年前後停火，涵蓋一八二一與一八二二兩個完整作戰季及其間的冬季。前線的地理骨架是幾條河與一條山脊：阿拉斯河是奧斯曼與波斯的實際分界，庫拉河構成高加索內側的界線；陸路方面，卡爾斯至埃爾祖魯姆公路約二百公里，德黑蘭至大不里士約二百五十公里，大不里士至卡爾斯約六百公里，補給全靠這條長線。兵員方面，兩造野戰兵力的具體數字在當時記述中相差頗大，通行說法多落在數萬量級：波斯方面以部落民兵湊集，人數看似龐大，裝備與指揮卻不統一；奧斯曼方面是常備步兵加民兵，編制較整齊。火繩槍的技術參數亦可推算：有效射程通常在一百步上下，至多二百步，單兵每分鐘只能射出數發，一個營的一次齊射約在數十秒內完成 - 這意味著齊射的整齊度比射程更要緊。火藥、鉛彈與糧食的輸送距離常超過三百公里，冬令封山時更形惡劣。至於各戰役的確切傷亡、俘虜與損失槍械數目，兩造戰史都沒有留下可核實的記載，諸說並存，本文因此不列任何具體傷亡數字。
dataEn: Few figures in this war can be verified, and the following are the more reliable ones. The fighting began in 1821 and wound down around 1823, covering two full campaigning seasons, 1821 and 1822, with the winter between them. The geographical skeleton of the front was a few rivers and one mountain chain: the Aras was the actual dividing line between the two empires, and the Kura formed the inner Caucasian boundary. On the roads, Kars to Erzurum is about two hundred kilometres, Tehran to Tabriz about two hundred and fifty, and Tabriz to Kars about six hundred; the whole of the supply of the eastern army travelled that long line. As for the size of the field armies, the numbers given in the contemporary accounts vary a great deal and the usual formulation is that both sides fielded several tens of thousands: Persia assembled its strength from tribal levies, which looked enormous on paper but were badly equipped and even more badly directed, while the Ottomans combined regular infantry with provincial auxiliaries on a tighter footing. The technical figures of the matchlock can be reasoned out: the effective range was normally around one hundred paces, at most two hundred; a single man could fire only a few rounds a minute; a battalion's volley was delivered within a matter of seconds. That makes regularity of the volley far more important than range. Powder, ball and food commonly travelled over three hundred kilometres, and the closing of the passes in winter made it worse. As for the exact losses in men, prisoners and broken firearms in individual actions, neither side's own war record leaves anything that can be checked, and the stories conflict; this account therefore quotes no casualty figures at all.
cause: 打起上來的緣由有三層。第一層是地緣：一八一三年《古利斯坦條約》把巴庫、嘉尼、卡拉巴赫、希爾萬、德朗特、庫巴、塔利斯等高加索汗國交予俄羅斯，波斯自此失去高加索的緩衝；對奧斯曼來說，那本就是自家勢力範圍內的附庸地，被俄國取走等於側翼被撬開。第二層是戰機：奧斯曼自一八〇六至一八一二年的俄土戰爭與拿破崙戰爭中抽身，一八一九年希臘人起義又牽住大量兵力，到一八二一年可調動的東方向軍隊有限，但窗口已經打開 - 俄國正忙於歐洲與中亞，無力干涉亞美尼亞。第三層是波斯的算盤：卡札爾王朝初立、財政吃緊，亟需一場勝利來鞏固王朝，並維繫邊區汗國的效忠；同時英國唯恐俄國勢力沿裏海與中亞南下，願意在外交上替波斯撐腰，令德黑蘭敢於與奧斯曼全面開戰。宗教上，什葉派波斯與遜尼派奧斯曼的對立提供了號召的旗號，但真正推動戰車的，是領土、稅源與王朝安全三件事。戰前波斯內部改革派阿布巴克里汗的去留與葉爾穆罕德沙的回朝，加劇了宮廷的猜疑，也讓部分地方勢力倒向奧斯曼。
causeEn: The reasons for the war run in three layers. The first is geography: the Treaty of Gulistan of 1813 handed the Caucasian khanates of Baku, Ganja, Karabakh, Shirvan, Derbent, Quba and Talysh over to Russia, and Persia from that moment lost its buffer in the Caucasus. For the Ottomans those khanates had long been client territory inside their own sphere of influence, and Russia's taking of them was read as a wedge driven into the Ottoman flank. The second is opportunity: released from the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812 and from the Napoleonic Wars, and further distracted by the Greek rising of 1819, the Ottomans had only limited forces to spare in the east in 1821, but the window was open, for Russia was absorbed in Europe and Central Asia and could not intervene in Armenia. The third is the Persian calculation: the Qajar dynasty was young and its finances were thin, and it badly needed a victory to shore up the dynasty and to hold the allegiance of the frontier khanates; at the same time Britain, alarmed at Russian expansion towards the Caspian and Central Asia, was willing to prop Persia up diplomatically and to let Tehran risk a general war with the Ottomans. Religiously, the Shia Persian and Sunni Ottoman divide gave a banner to rally around, but what really moved the war was territory, taxes and the security of the dynasty. Before the fighting began, the fate of the reformer Abu Bakr Khan at the Persian court and the return of Yermolov sharpened the suspicion in the palace, and pushed some of the local powers towards the Ottomans.
impact: 這場戰爭沒有分出勝負，卻改變了高加索的命運。波斯的守成意味著附庸汗國繼續留在俄國手中；一八二六至一八二八年俄國大舉南下，《土庫曼恰伊條約》把巴庫、嘉尼、卡拉巴赫、希爾萬與德朗特正式割予俄國，波斯就此失去裏海西岸的門戶，石油與絲綢貿易的走向亦隨之轉移，卡札爾王室的財政與軍備愈來愈倚賴英國的貸款與英國顧問的設計。奧斯曼的戰果同樣有限：它沒有從俄國或波斯手上取得任何持久的高加索立足點，反而在戰後被希臘起義與俄土戰爭雙雙拖住；一八二七年它雖趁俄國在波斯用兵之際一度奪回埃里溫，一八二九年《亞得里亞堡條約》後仍被迫歸還。在軍事技術上，兩軍都從這一役學到同一課：火繩槍可以守城、可以列陣，卻救不了斷絕的糧道與混亂的指揮；波斯的火繩槍步兵與新式砲兵在這幾年裡得到一次難得的鍛鍊，日後卡札爾王朝的軍制改革 - 線形步兵、製式火槍軍械與集中的砲兵營 - 可看出這段經驗的痕跡。經濟上，波斯西部的道路中斷，大不里士的絲綢與裏海沿岸的糧食運銷受損，軍費與歉收疊在一起，重壓阿爾達比勒與大不里士一帶，使改革派的財政理想與王室的軍費爭奪更加尖銳。
impactEn: The war settled nothing, yet it changed the fate of the Caucasus. Persia's stalemate meant that the client khanates stayed in Russian hands; when Russia marched south in 1826-1828 the Treaty of Turkmenchay formally ceded Baku, Ganja, Karabakh, Shirvan and Derbent to the empire, Persia lost the door on the western Caspian for good, and the direction of the oil and silk trade moved with it, while the finances and armament of the Qajar court came to lean ever more heavily on British loans and on British advice. The Ottoman results were equally limited: no durable Caucasian foothold was gained from either Russia or Persia, and the empire was immediately pulled in two directions by the Greek rising and by the next Russo-Turkish War. It seized Erivan from the Russians in 1827 while Russia was campaigning in Persia, but had to hand it back after the Treaty of Adrianople of 1829. In military terms both armies learnt the same lesson: the matchlock could hold a town and could fight in line, but it could not rescue a cut supply line or a confused command. Persia's matchlock infantry and its new artillery received a rare hardening in these years, and the later Qajar military reforms - linear infantry, standard issue muskets and centralised artillery parks - carry the trace of that experience. Economically the roads of western Persia were cut, the silk of Tabriz and the grain trade along the Caspian suffered, and military costs piled on top of poor harvests, weighing on Ardabil and Tabriz and sharpening the quarrel between the reformers' fiscal programme and the court's war spending.
result: 打到最後，雙方都沒有拿到想要的東西：奧斯曼未能佔領埃里溫與嘉尼一帶的核心，波斯也未能把汗國收回，戰線在一八二三年前後大致回到開戰前的樣子。造成這個結局的直接原因是消耗 - 高加索的冬季、漫長的補給線、攻城重砲不足所限制的攻城能力，以及雙方在另一條戰線上同時受困：奧斯曼被希臘起義拖住，波斯則要提防阿富汗方向。關於此役的具體經過與結條，兩造記載互相矛盾、諸說並存；可以確定的是雙方在疲憊中默認停火，並未留下完整可靠的正式和約文本，因此學界多以「恢復戰前狀態」概括其結果。真正決定這片土地歸屬的，是三年後的俄波戰爭（一八二六至一八二八年）與其後的《土庫曼恰伊條約》；本役對卡札爾王朝最深的影響，或許不是失地，而是讓德黑蘭看清一件事 - 以部落騎兵為骨架的軍隊，無論騎術多嫻熟，也守不住高山要塞與裏海口岸，火繩槍所代表的成建制步兵與配合的砲兵，才是能真正改變戰局的東西。
resultEn: In the end neither side gained what it wanted. The Ottomans failed to take the heart of Erivan and Ganja, Persia failed to recover the khanates, and by about 1823 the front had returned to roughly the position it had held before the war began. The direct reason for this outcome was exhaustion: the winter in the Caucasus, the long supply line, the sieges that limited artillery could carry, and the fact that both armies were pinned on another front as well, the Ottomans by the Greek rising and Persia by the Afghan border. The detailed course of the campaign and its terms are recorded contradictorily on the two sides, and the stories conflict; what can be established is that the two armies fell back into an informal ceasefire out of exhaustion, that no complete and reliable formal peace text survives, and that for this reason the general custom is to summarise the result as a return to the status quo before the war. What really decided the ownership of this land was the Russo-Persian War three years later, 1826-1828, and the Treaty of Turkmenchay that followed it. The deepest effect of this war on the Qajar dynasty may not have been the loss of territory, but the lesson it taught Tehran: an army built on tribal cavalry, however expert in the saddle, could not hold the mountain fortresses or the Caspian shore, and it was the drilled infantry and the supporting artillery represented by the matchlock that could truly change the course of a war.
